chapter: New York 1936-39 (second pass of the transcript)
title: Bands opposite Chick Webb and Jesse Owens's band (second pass)
summary: Repeat of the bands at the Savoy and the failed Jesse Owens band.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money

blocks.x: Yeah. To go back to the Savoy, what other bands did you play opposite besides Chick Webb?
Whoever came in there. Tommy Dorsey, Buddy Barrigan, Erskine Hawkins, Teddy Hill, even what's the champion runner for Munich, Hitler --
He had a band, he had a band and,
oh, this is a funny bit. He had a band and they were trying to promote him as --
Right after the olympics, I guess?

Yeah, and they were trying to promote him as a bandleader and he knows nothing about the business nor his promoters and he's hired New York musicians and you have rehearsal, and you can get a draw -- how can you get a draw today and don't show tomorrow, or ever.
So, how did he finally put a band in there?
Well, it just fell apart. It just fell apart.
Was it a regular big band?
Yeah, it was a big band. It had to be a big band because he was replacing Chick Webb.
Co you remember who played in that band then?

Everybody, when they found out that you could get a draw, you know, they were hard times. There was no place -- we weren't working below 110th Street at that period of time. It wasn't until '39, '37 that the spiritual rhythm --
